title: The Monty Hall Problem
summary: On a game show there are three doors: a car behind one, goats behind the other two. You pick a door; the host, who knows where the car is, opens one of the others to show a goat, and offers you the chance to switch. Most people feel it's now fifty-fifty, but switching wins two times in three: your first pick is right only a third of the time, and when it's wrong the host's choice leaves the car behind the other door. Steve Selvin posed it in 1975; when Marilyn vos Savant gave the answer in Parade magazine in 1990, thousands of readers, many with PhDs, wrote in to say she was wrong.
citations: Steve Selvin, "A Problem in Probability," letter to the editor, The American Statistician 29, no. 1 (1975): 67
Steve Selvin, "On the Monty Hall Problem," The American Statistician 29, no. 3 (1975): 134
reading: Jason Rosenhouse, The Monty Hall Problem (Oxford University Press, 2009)
